acknowledged.reason: Each reads a different runner's session file format (Claude Code JSONL vs Codex rollout). They look alike because both walk lines, but their fields and events differ and change independently with each CLI; a runner is its own reader (RunnerSpec).
Same names, different jobs: agents speaks Claude Code's live stream-json protocol, sessions reads its saved session files. Different inputs, crates and rules (sessions is read-only, no processes).

Two cleaners for different outputs: core's shown keeps any text up to a length; sessions' title_text takes only a title's first line. The sessions crate may use only core's runner and activity modules (CLAUDE.md), so it cannot import core's helper.

Opposite on purpose: plain turns line breaks into spaces (one line, for labels); kept_text keeps them as newlines (what a capture stores). A shared helper would need a flag that hides which one a caller wants.
Colour tables for different things: station colours the dial's stations, accent is the one colour that follows the mode (status pill, focused pane). Changing one must not change the other.
Coincidental shape: State.group picks a task's sidebar heading, pulse picks the dial centre's colour for an agent's state. Different decisions that happen to be small matches.
Two different native controls (a push button; a checkbox that can be disabled and read back) for the canary test app. Each needs its own AppKit setup; a shared helper would only hide the differences.

Both fetch the view's window and change one setting, but different settings for different reasons: one stops native full screen (so app windows can still be hosted), the other floats the e2e window above others.
